_comment: UNVERIFIED, pending a native speaker and a musician. A transition is CONSTRAINED only when the melody moves at least melodyMoveSemitones and the voice moves at least speechMoveLevels (Chao levels) between the two syllables; anything else is neither a pass nor a fail and is reported as unconstrained. A melody is ELIGIBLE only if, across its phrases, at least minMovingFraction of adjacent note pairs move and its range spans at least minRangeSemitones; below that it is reported as ineligible, never as optimal, because a drone avoids every test. A setting is eligible only if the melody engages (constrains) at least minConstrainedFraction of the transitions where the VOICE moves; transitions where the voice is flat are not in the denominator because no melody can engage them. This stops an alignment winning by parking tone changes on repeated notes.

ask: For a tune to count as a real melody rather than a chant: is it enough that half of its note-to-note steps move, over a range of five semitones (a fourth)?
For a setting to count as tested: is it enough that the tune moves on half of the places where the spoken tones change?
Is any change of note (one semitone) a real move for a singer, or should very small steps count as flat?
